moat_against: Commodity-like IV fluids; hospital/GPO buyers hold pricing power vs Fresenius Kabi, B. Braun and other rivals
ROIC collapsed 2019-2025 (14.14% to -1.78%, negative in 2022 and 2025) and gross margin fell ~12pp — no demonstrated pricing power
Hillrom moat overpaid for: ~$3.1B of impairments within a year of the 2021 acquisition
Quality/supply erosion: Novum IQ hold, pump field corrective actions, Helene disruption, injectables constraints
moat_for: Largest IV solutions supplier in North America with an extensive manufacturing network
Installed base of infusion pumps and Hillrom hospital beds creating consumables, service and replacement pull-through
Mission-critical, regulated products with long hospital qualification cycles and switching friction
Scale across IV, compounding, advanced surgery and connected care
moat_justification: Largest U.S. IV solutions supplier with an installed pump and Hillrom bed base and regulated, mission-critical products, but commodity-like core categories, GPO pricing pressure, and ROIC that collapsed from 14.14% in 2019 to -1.78% in 2025 (5.25% / -10.78% / 2.77% / 0.06% / -1.78% over 2021-2025, fundamentals.json) with gross margin down from 41.90% to 30.05% — no measured pricing power to justify a higher score.
name: Baxter International Inc.
one_liner: Levered hospital-supplies incumbent, moat 4/10 — even on recovered TTM owner's earnings it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 7.4%, IV@15% $10.04 vs $25.28 price); it clears 15% only below ~$10.04.
